subject: maths
title: Substitution Sanctuary
description: Use u-substitution to unlock tricky integrals.

concepts.def: Let u = inner function; rewrite integral in terms of u and du.
Often pick u as the 'inside' whose derivative appears.
For definite integrals, transform limits to u values too.
∫(2x+1)⁵ dx with u=2x+1, du=2dx; gives (2x+1)⁶/12 + C.
f'(x)·f(x)ⁿ, f'(x)/f(x), and e^(f(x))·f'(x) all substitution-friendly.

walkthroughs.body_html:
u = x²+1, du = 2x dx

∫ u³ du = u⁴/4 = (x²+1)⁴/4 + C

u = 3x, du = 3dx

(1/3)∫ cos u du = (1/3) sin 3x + C

u = x²+1, du = 2x dx

(1/2)∫ du/u = (1/2)ln|x²+1| + C
